Earth turns anticlockwise under the Sun, seen from above the North Pole. The outer ring of solar hours stays still, with noon facing the Sun; the 24 time zones of 15° turn with Earth, and six cities carry the time of their zone. On the right, a clock for each city. The *Speed* slider sets how many hours pass in one second, ❚❚ pauses and *Now* goes back to the present time.

## What to look for

- How many degrees does Earth turn in one hour? In four minutes?
- When it is noon in London, what time is it in Neuchâtel, New York and Tokyo? Why?
- Which city sees the Sun rise first, New York or Mumbai?
- Mumbai's clock is not on a whole hour: why might a country choose a zone of half an hour?

## How it works

Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, so 15° per hour: every 15° to the east, noon comes one hour earlier. The 24 nominal zones are 15° wide; the cities show the standard time of their real zone, without summer time. Day and night are drawn as at an equinox.
